Subject: Production SLA expectations for national rollout

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the product demo this week. We had a quick internal sync and Medivest is preparing to go live with Redwood in three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) in July. Before we finalize procurement we need clarity on two items:

1) Uptime target and tolerated variance across regions — our security team has pushed for a 99.95% uptime commitment per region.
2) Remedy and service credit structure in case of regional degradation, and whether Redwood will accept a unified multi-regional SLA (credits calculated per incident vs aggregated).

Attached is a short spreadsheet with the target windows and traffic estimates. Our procurement lead (cc'd) asked if you can propose a clean exception path if you cannot meet 99.95 in all regions on day one.

Can we get a proposed wording and any required executive signoff windows by next week?

Best,
Sarah Connor
Head of Platform Operations
Medivest Health

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clarity and the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can support a staged uptime commitment and an exception for the initial multiregional ramp, but it requires an explicit remedy cap and a documented rollout plan. I'll loop in Deal Desk and legal to put a specific exhibit together.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll share an updated SLA excerpt that defines a ramped uptime tolerance (99.8% for first 90 days in a new region, 99.95% thereafter) + a credits matrix tied to per-incident regional impact.
- If you accept the ramp, we will require executive signoff from Redwood for the exception and a small one-time onboarding fee credit to balance the commercial terms.

I'll send a draft by EOD Tuesday.

Aditya / Marissa —

Forwarding Medivest's ask. Key points: multiregional rollout July; they want 99.95% per region immediately. We can get to 99.95 once warmed, but first-90-days we expect some higher tail given cross-region caching and failover tuning.

Proposed position for Deal Desk:
- Offer a 90-day ramp: 99.8% (per region) for first 90 days after GA region launch, ramping to 99.95% thereafter.
- Remedy: service credits calculated per region per incident up to a maximum of 12% of monthly bill per month (instead of standard 25%).
- Commercial trade: 10% one-time onboarding credit if Medivest accepts the ramp and limits credits to 12% cap.

Marissa — can you confirm legal will accept the reduced cap and the ramp language as an Exhibit A amendment? Vivek — seeking executive signoff for the exception and the 10% onboarding concession.

Thanks,
Jasmine

Team —

Reviewed the proposed language. Legal is broadly comfortable with a staged uptime commitment provided that:
1) The ramp duration is explicit (90 days) and measured from date of first production traffic in each region.
2) Credits remain calculated on a per-incident basis and capped at 12% monthly, but we add an explicit exclusion for incidents caused by customer configuration or third-party network outages (to protect Redwood).
3) Add a clause: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to enable multiregional failover within 2 hours of detecting regional degradation, with a documented runbook. This is a performance commitment, not a contractual uptime guarantee.

I have redlined Exhibit A and attached the draft SLA excerpt. If the execs are okay with the lower cap and onboarding credit, legal will finalize the exhibit for signature.

Thanks for the summary. I approve the exception as proposed with the following business guardrails:
- Accept ramped regional uptime: 99.8% for first 90 days, target 99.95% thereafter.
- Remedy cap: 12% monthly credit cap (per account), credits calculated per-incident.
- Commercial concession: 10% one-time onboarding credit applied against month-1 invoice.
- Additional: The exception applies only to the initial production date per region; if a region is brought down for maintenance that exceeds scheduled windows, the standard SLA applies.

Please proceed to finalize Exhibit A and coordinate signature. Jasmine — include this approval note in the outbound to Medivest and call out the exclusions Marissa flagged.

Subject: Final: Multiregional uptime exception — Medivest onboarding terms

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for your patience. Per our internal review and executive signoff, Redwood can agree to the following exception for Medivest's multiregional rollout: 

Summary (final):
- Ramp: Each new production region will be covered by a 90-day ramp during which the regional uptime target is 99.8%. After the 90-day ramp, the standard regional target is 99.95%.
- Remedy: Service credits will be calculated per incident based on regional impact. Credits are capped at 12% of the monthly invoice (per account) for any given month.
- Exclusions: Incidents attributable to customer configuration errors, third-party network outages, or force majeure are excluded from credits.
- Failover commitment: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to enable multiregional failover within 2 hours of detection and maintain a published runbook for incident response (performance commitment only).
- Commercial: Redwood will apply a 10% one-time onboarding credit to the first invoice upon signature of the exhibit.

Next steps:
1) Attached is the redlined Exhibit A (redwood-sla-proposal-v3.pdf). Marissa's team will finalize language once you confirm acceptance of the exclusions.
2) If accepted, we'll issue a DocuSign package with Exhibit A and the purchase order terms.

Please reply with acceptance or any final concerns by EOD Wednesday so we can keep the July launch timeline.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
